presets.title: General
presets.what: The everyday preset: questions, writing, checking things, your own paperwork - one balanced setup instead of a separate admin preset. Since 2026-11-18 it is the 26B model at a 32,768-token window on the pooled three-card lane: the owner chose it on quality, after a blind battery of eight tasks scored it 22/24, the best of the four tried.
presets.cost: HEAVY MODE: it needs all three cards at once as ONE pooled lane (port 11450) and pauses the everyday 9B model while it loads. Measured on this PC on 2026-11-17 on that lane at 32,768 tokens: 15.50 GiB resident, 14.82 GiB in the cards' memory and 0.68 GiB spilled into system memory, 25.4 tokens a second (two runs read 25.4-36.5, the low end is shown) and a 49.9 s cold load.
presets.worse: It fills all three cards, so a preset that is not heavy stops its lane and brings the everyday 9B back; returning to General costs its cold load (about 50 seconds). The everyday lane is paused while it runs, so a chat arriving then waits for the switch. `ollama show` reports completion, vision, tools and thinking and a real 573M-parameter image projector, so pictures and tools are not lost - but its picture quality and its general, tool-calling and vision rubric results are NOT measured on this PC, so nothing here claims them. It thinks before it answers, so a short answer allowance can cut it off before it speaks.

presets.title: General Uncensored

presets.cost: Measured 2026-10-18: cold load 18.5-20.5 s, 45.6 tokens a second at 8k and 45-46 at 16k; 32k loads 7.3 GB at 100% GPU (it only splits across cards when others are resident; no CPU spill). 6.3 GB on disk, Apache-2.0, Qwen3.5 family, 8.95B parameters.

presets.title: Coding
presets.what: For writing and fixing code, reading a project, and long tool-driven coding jobs: the 30B coding model on ONE lane that sees all three cards, started on demand by this apply.
presets.cost: HEAVY MODE: it fills ALL THREE GPUs (16.17 GiB of video memory here, with the same q8_0 cache the everyday lane uses, and nothing pushed into system RAM) and pauses the everyday model while it works, for about 32 s on a cold load. Measured 2026-11-07 at 49,152 tokens on all three cards: 83.8 tokens a second after a 900-word prompt, prompt ~1,644 tokens a second, zero CPU spill. The same-night two-card control (same q8_0 cache) at 32,768 tokens read 60.6 tokens a second with a 69.6 s cold load; the 2026-11-03 shipped record used the default f16 cache and read 80.4 at a 36.0 s load, so it is not a like-for-like baseline. Against the control the three-card window is about 38% faster; against the older record the gain is small - the real change is the 16,384-token wider window with zero spill and no spill allowance. The older figures (76.2 tok/s at 28,672; 80.4 at 32,768 with 323.5 MiB spilled) are kept in docs/MEASURED-2026-11-07-THREE-GPU.md.
presets.worse: Applying it makes it the model chat uses, so the everyday 26B is NOT resident while it runs - it comes back when you apply another preset, and that switch costs its cold load (about 50 seconds since 2026-11-18). It is not a quick helper: it takes all three cards for as long as it is on, and nothing else can be loaded beside it. Measured about 59 tokens a second at 65,536 tokens, so the wider window is not offered.

measured.source: measurement 2026-11-07 on all three cards with OLLAMA_SCHED_SPREAD=1: 49,152 tokens loaded at 16.2 GiB entirely in video memory, 83.8 tok/s warm generation after a 900-word prompt, prompt ~1,644 tok/s, cold load 31.6 s, three cards used (nvidia-smi deltas). The same-night two-card control (q8_0, 32,768 tokens) measured 60.58 tok/s with a 69.611 s cold load and zero spill as well; the 2026-11-03 shipped record used the default f16 cache and read 80.36 tok/s at a 36.0 s load, so the two baselines are not comparable. 65,536 tokens measured 59.06 tok/s and 98,304 measured 88.69 tok/s, both with zero spill; 49,152 is the larger of the two windows the Q2 ruling named (49,152 and 65,536) that clears the 75 tok/s bar - 98,304 was outside those windows and is recorded, not chosen. The 6/6 coding rubric was measured 2026-10-18 on two cards and was not re-run. Evidence: docs/MEASURED-2026-11-07-THREE-GPU.md and .dsh-scratch/GPU-3WAY-2026-11-06/bench/results3/.

presets.title: Fast
presets.what: The quickest preset: qwen3.5:4b at the 16,384-token window it is for, on the everyday lane. Since 2026-11-18 there is no separate fast card: applying it makes qwen3.5:4b the model chat uses, and going back to General asks the lane for the everyday 26B again.
presets.cost: Measured 2026-10-10 on an RTX 2080 SUPER: 77.1 tokens a second and 4.15 GB of video memory at a 65,536-token window (the file is 3.16 GB on disk). Since 2026-11-18 the everyday lane spans all three cards, so that figure is the model's measurement on this PC rather than a fresh one for the lane; this row keeps the 16,384-token window it is for.
presets.worse: The small model: fastest measured writer here, and the bench's three short prompts were only called broadly correct rather than scored. Chosen for waiting less, not for care. The 26B does not fit beside it on the same three cards, so switching back to General costs the everyday model's cold load (about 50 seconds).

presets.title: Reflective Coach
presets.what: For talking something through: a calm listener that reflects what you said first and asks one gentle question at a time. Since 2026-11-18 it thinks on all three cards at once, so a difficult thought gets the whole machine instead of one card.
presets.cost: HEAVY MODE: it needs all three cards at once as one pooled lane and pauses the everyday and Fast models while it thinks. Measured on this PC on 2026-11-09: 15.5 GiB loaded with 0.68 GiB (4.4%) spilled into system memory, 96% in the cards' memory, a 52.0 s cold load and 49.26 tokens a second. No model on this PC has been measured for empathy or reflective quality, and nothing here claims it.
presets.worse: A model choice only - it changes no wording by itself. It is not a therapist: it gives no diagnosis, keeps no therapy record and the crisis help stays exactly where it already is. Applying it pauses the other models for about a minute, so it is for a session of thinking, not for a quick question.

presets.title: Medical Expert
presets.what: For reading clinical material carefully and in calm plain words: lab panels, letters, medication lists and health questions. It is a purpose-trained medical model on all three cards at once. It is not a doctor, gives no diagnosis and replaces no clinician.
presets.cost: HEAVY MODE: it needs all three cards at once (17.31 GiB loaded entirely in video memory, 0 B spilled) and pauses the everyday and Fast models while it runs. It is slow: a 46.8 s cold load and 9.27 tokens a second on the measured coding prompt (11.1 on the measured ~150-word explanation, 7.89 on the four-token answer), so a long answer takes a while. Measured on this PC on 2026-11-09 (model-bench run 20261109-105956, the medgemma window row).
presets.worse: It has NO tool calling - `ollama show` reports no `tools` capability, so it cannot use Jarvis's tools, browser or files. It reports vision (pictures), but its picture quality is not measured here. It is not a doctor: no diagnosis, no prescription and no replacement for your own clinician, and a model trained on clinical text can still be wrong about your case.

recommendations.basis: one preset's model is loaded at a time; every heavy preset, General included, needs the pooled lane's three cards, so one- and two-card layouts are reasoned and labelled, never claimed as measured

three_gpu_plan.layout: ONE preset's model is loaded at a time: applying another preset ends the previous one first, so no preset has to keep a card free for another. The everyday lane (port 11436) is ONE card on this PC and serves the 9B rows - Documents & Notes and Browser & Forms at 196,608 tokens, Fast and Agentic + Vision at 16,384. The pooled lane (port 11450) sees ALL THREE cards and carries every heavy preset - General's 26B at 32,768, Coding, Reflective Coach, Pictures & Screens and Medical - and it pauses the everyday model while it runs, because no preset has to keep a card free for another. So any preset may use all three cards where its model warrants it. There is no one-lane-per-GPU split any more.

three_gpu_plan.heavy_pooled: on demand, a heavy preset pauses the everyday model and loads ONE model on the pooled lane on port 11450 across all the cards: General (gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat at 32,768), Coding (qwen3-coder-30b-a3b-ud-q3-k-xl at 49,152 tokens), Medical (medgemma:27b at 32,768), Reflective Coach (gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat at 32,768) and Pictures & Screens (qwen3-vl-30b-a3b-instruct at 32,768). Each is too big for one card, which is why a heavy preset splits one model across the cards; every preset that is not heavy runs on the one everyday lane, one model at a time.
three_gpu_plan.link_note: the third card likely sits on the B550 chipset through an M.2 adapter: PCIe 3.0 x4, maybe x2. A slower link costs loading time, not a lane: the everyday model is loaded once across all three cards, so the link is paid at load, not per token.
three_gpu_plan.future_not_a_preset: Qwen3.8-27B pooled to 28 GB across cards is a future 'max quality' experiment only; it is not a preset and no figure is claimed until it is measured.
